prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
 No named child cast: Kit and Zoe MUST NOT appear. Include unnamed human workers/adults ONLY when explicitly required by this particular scene; otherwise show only the natural subjects. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Vehicles That Fly; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: Factual daylight aircraft views with no recurring children. Plane: plain white twin-engine passenger jet with teal tail, fixed wings and both engine nacelles under wings. Helicopter: orange civilian craft with a four-blade main rotor, enclosed cabin, tail rotor and two skids. Balloon: broad yellow fabric envelope with three blue vertical panels, dark burner frame, tan basket and one adult pilot wearing a plain gray jacket. Keep aircraft types distinct; safe separated flight areas; no flags, brands or military details.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): White passenger jet with teal tail; Orange four-blade helicopter; Yellow-and-blue hot-air balloon with burner and tan basket
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: Opening comparison; all three aircraft whole and clearly separated.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: Three-part comparison diagram: white teal-tailed jet angled gently upward at left, orange helicopter level at right and yellow-blue balloon rising at center above low fields. Clearly separate the aircraft; no close formation or collision path.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions. Reference-sheet override: any lettering requested by the opening page brief belongs only in that finished page. Keep this production reference board entirely unlabelled; no letters, numbers or pseudo-writing.

visualReview.note: Aircraft and pilot design board; fixed-wing white/teal jet, four-bladed orange helicopter and yellow/blue balloon stay distinct. Producer independently inspected the final installed WebP natively; complete final sequence and relevant native diagrams were independently reviewed.
